parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why the gravitational potential near to a point mass is negative.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A planet may be assumed to be a uniform sphere. It has gravitational potential *φ* at distance *r* from the centre of the planet.

The variation with $\frac{1}{r}$ of *φ* is shown in Fig. 1.1.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: Show that the mass of the planet is 8.8 × 10²⁵ kg.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The period of rotation of the planet is 0.72 Earth days.

A satellite in orbit around the planet remains above the same point on the surface of the planet.

Use the mass of the planet in (b)(i) to determine the radius *R* of the orbit of the satellite.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The speed of the satellite in (b)(ii) is 8400 m s⁻¹. The mass of the satellite is 1200 kg.

Determine the additional energy required to move the satellite from its orbit to infinity.

figures.caption: Fig. 1.1
figures.alt: A graph of gravitational potential against 1/r, with both axes marked on a grid and a straight line sloping down from the origin.
